'''''Montanoa hibiscifolia''''', the '''tree daisy''' or '''Anzac-flower''', is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Asteraceae]].<ref name="commonnames_Mh" >{{cite web |url=https://identify.plantnet.org/k-world-flora/species/Montanoa%20hibiscifolia%20Benth./data-newMh |title=''Montanoa hibiscifolia'' Benth. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=22 February 2024 |website=plantnet.org |publisher=Pl@ntNet |access-date=31 March 2024 |quote=Validated names 4; Anzac-flower, Tree daisy, Treedaisy, Mallow-leaf Montanoa }}</ref> It is native to Central America and southern Mexico, and it has been introduced to other locations including South Africa and Australia.<ref name="POWO_164002-2" >{{cite POWO |id=164002-2 |title=''Montanoa hibiscifolia'' Benth. |access-date=31 March 2024 }}</ref> An erect tree-like perennial reaching {{cvt|6|m}}, it is invasive, capable of forming dense stands.<ref name="commonnames_Mh" /><ref name="CABI_34787" >{{cite journal |title=''Montanoa hibiscifolia'' (Tree daisy) |date=2022 |journal=CABI Compendium |doi=10.1079/cabicompendium.34787 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Description== 
[[File:Starr-081230-0669-Montanoa hibiscifolia-flowers and leaves-Upper Kaulana-Kahoolawe (24927251115).jpg|thumb|left|Shrub formation]]
It is an erect, tree-like, perennial shrub that is {{cvt|2|to|7|m|ft|0}} tall.<ref name="commonnames_Mh" /><ref name="CABI_34787" /> [[Leaf arrangement]] is simple and their form is opposite. They are [[pinnatifid]] when young, and [[palmate]]ly lobed during maturity. The leaves are up to {{cvt|25|cm|in|0}} in length and width, dark green above and paler below, and smoothly hairy on both surfaces, with a pair of lobes at the base of the leaf blade.<ref name=bris/> 

===Inflorescences===
Daisy-like flowers, which appear from late autumn to winter, are approximately {{cvt|4|cm|in|0}} across. The ray petals or [[floret]]s are white in color with a yellow disc. The flowers appear abundantly in [[panicle|terminal]] branched [[inflorescence]]s. The disc florets are green but turn yellow. Reddish-brown dry fruits appear like old chartaceous flower heads, one-seeded, which do not open to release the seed.<ref name=bris>{{cite web |url=https://weeds.brisbane.qld.gov.au/weeds/anzac-tree-daisy |title=Anzac tree daisy |publisher=[[Brisbane City Council]] |access-date=13 December 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Montanoa~hibiscifolia |title=''Montanoa hibiscifolia'' (Benth.) Schultz |publisher=PlantNET |access-date=13 December 2024 }}</ref>

==Distribution==
It is native to Central America (Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua) and southern Mexico, and it has been introduced to other locations including South Africa and Australia.<ref name="POWO_164002-2" >{{cite POWO |id=164002-2 |title=''Montanoa hibiscifolia'' Benth. |access-date=31 March 2024 }}</ref> 

It has been cultivated as a [[garden plant]], though it has since [[escaped plant|escaped cultivation]] and has become a weed at [[road verge]]s, [[riparian zone]]s, [[savanna]]s, river banks, [[gully|gullies]] and [[forest edge]]s. It is invasive, capable of forming dense stands, and is therefore listed as a noxious weed in places such as South Africa and Hawaii, in addition to being a sleeper weed in southeastern [[Queensland]]. It has been naturalized in [[Norfolk Island]], [[Réunion|La Reunion]], the coastal districts of northern [[New South Wales]], and [[French Polynesia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://keyserver.lucidcentral.org/weeds/data/media/Html/montanoa_hibiscifolia.htm |title=''Montanoa hibiscifolia'' Benth. |publisher=Lucid Central |access-date=13 December 2024 }}</ref> 

Propagation and reproduction occurs chiefly from seeds, which are [[Seed dispersal|dispersed]] by travelling vehicles and waterflows.<ref name=bris/>
